notes: Defoliation reduced both CH and CL fruit production and more strongly reduced CH. Pollination enhancement had no main effect on CH or CL production; the significant interaction buffered the CH damage effect. This supports context-dependent route sensitivity but not a direct receipt that pollination and herbivory push one shared CH-vs-CL allocation decision in opposite directions.

Moderate florivory reduced the proportion of reproduction from CH flowers and increased relative selfed reproduction, but the source did not manipulate pollination as an opposing demand and could not distinguish altered CL production from differential fruit maturation. Mixed mating and route shift are real; BALANCE conflict is not identified.

source_basis: Krupnick & Weis 1999 Ecology 80:135-149; Krupnick, Weis & Campbell 1999 Ecology 80:125-134
notes: The primary programme quantifies herbivory effects on pollinator service, pollen export, pollen receipt, fruit and seed production in an andromonoecious species. It does not demonstrate that male versus hermaphroditic flower allocation is the route through which a shared functional conflict is resolved.

Damage altered growth/clonal responses, but pollination did not affect growth, clone production, or flower production in the reported experiments. Sexual and asexual routes therefore form a useful specificity case rather than a demonstrated opposing-demand routing system.
